cells.tense: What survived the clearing is settled, and you are still sorting it.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: With someone you trust, run one exchange both ways this week: offer what you'd offer anyway, then accept what comes back without deflecting it.
cells.core:
You know the difference between keeping something and gripping it, and you've been keeping. What you carried out of the collapse is standing, and you can tell which parts deserve the shelf space and which are just loud. A friend asks for something and you hand it over, and you take what they hand back. That part is unhurried in you.

Pick someone you trust and run one exchange both ways. Offer what you'd have offered anyway, then accept what comes back without deflecting it. Fairness won't run out here. You'll know the rhythm has you when passing something across stops feeling like a toll you pay to stay.
cells.sheetLine: The ground is new, and it holds what you chose.
cells.verb: holding what the change left standing
cells.place: a room the collapse has emptied and stopped heating

cells.tense: You are bracing for a clearing that already came and went.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Let one thing tug at you this week and go partway toward it without deciding anything yet — just look, and stay undecided.
cells.core:
You keep guarding a space that's already empty. The clearing happened a while back, and you're still in the doorway with a hand up, scanning for the next collapse. Your grip on what survived has gone past keeping into bracing, and it's showing in how you hold everything at arm's length.

Something new is tugging at you, and it isn't the old thing tugging. Let one thing pull at you this week and go partway toward it without deciding anything yet. Just look, and stay undecided. The brace eases when your attention has somewhere ahead to land, and this already has somewhere to land.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door the clearing already opened.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: Name the direction you already chose, once, to yourself. The next time something pushes against it, keep that heading and don't move off it.
cells.core:
There's a version of you that knows what you kept and can say why without reaching. Someone questions it and you answer from the thing itself, not from defense. That version exists and lately you're not in it.

The old structure is gone and you're waiting for the room to settle before you step in. You decided something and haven't named it yet, so nothing carries it but habit. Name the direction once, to yourself, and keep that heading the next time something pushes against it. Just that one push, refused. What you kept needs a defender before it needs a plan, and the defender is you, standing where you already are.

cells.tense: You are setting things straight without knowing that you are the one doing it.
cells.act: let the structure act instead of announcing it
cells.ask: Next time you quietly put something back in order, let the action carry it with no explanation to anyone, then notice afterward that you did it.
cells.core:
Ask anyone and the space sorts itself out. It doesn't; someone keeps it clear, and that someone is you. You're firm about what matters day to day, and the quiet of this room moves like it belongs to the room rather than to you. That version is right. The record just doesn't carry your name.

Next time you quietly set something back in order, let the action do the work with no explanation, and then notice afterward that you did it. Not a speech to anyone. Just knowing, once, that the calm here is yours to lay down or pick up on purpose.
cells.sheetLine: The calm in this room is yours. It isn't credited to you.
